rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on gods besides God challenges them to reproduce something God established or undo one of His acts.
rows.anchor: لشيء مما أثبته سبحانه لنفسه فليفعلوا شيئا مثله أو يبطلو شيئا مما فعله سبحانه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their silence betrays inability and confusion, so God supplies the answer; an attentive person would have no hesitation in answering.
rows.anchor: ولما كان جوابهم في ذلك السكوت عجزا وحيرة , تواى سبحانه الجواب عنهم , إشارة إلى أن جواب كل من له تأمل لا وقفة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As another possibility, God answers for them because some beings claimed as gods may possess knowledge.
rows.anchor: أو لأن بعض من ادعيت إلآهيته ممن له علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The false gods neither own anything now nor will ever acquire any of the denied power.
rows.anchor: أي الآن ولا يتجدد لهم شيء من ذلك أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tiny weight of a mote hyperbolically expresses utter insignificance in terms familiar to Arabs.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المراد المبالغة في الحقارة بما تعرف العرب قال : { مثقال ذرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heaven and earth encompass everything high and low, including all entities and meanings within them up to the Throne.
rows.anchor: فاستغرق ذلك النفي عنهما وعن كل ما فيهما من ذات ومعنى إلى العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse separately denies the alleged gods any share in creation or ownership, even of themselves and their powers, so they cannot help anyone.
rows.anchor: أي في خلق ولا ملك ولا ملك , وقد انتفى ملكهم لشيء من أنفسهم أو ما أسكن فيها سبحانه من قوة أو منفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no helper among them in anything He wills; their total incapacity makes invocation, hope, and worship of them incoherent.
rows.anchor: أي معين على شيء مما يريده , فكيف يصح مع هذا العجز الكلي أن يدعوا كما يدعى ويرجوا كما يرجى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining alleged benefit, intercession, cannot benefit anyone with God except one for whom permission is granted.
rows.anchor: ولما كان قد بقي من أقسام النفع الشفاعة , وكان المقصود منها أثرها لا عينها , نفاه بقوله

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read the permission clause passively, making the verbal noun the grammatical subject and allowing permission through an intermediary of God's choosing.
rows.anchor: قال في قراءة أبي عمرو وحمزة والكسائي بجعل المصدر عمدة الكلام وإسناد الفعل إليه : { أذن له }

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: They read the clause actively: God Himself must explicitly authorize intercession, and no one can overreach Him.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الباقين بالبناء للفاعل تدل على العظمة من وجه آخر , وهو أنه لا افتيات عليه بوجه من أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording of the removal clause heightens the awe and veiling of the terrifying assembly where intercessors and beneficiaries are overwhelmed.
rows.anchor: فلذلك كان من المعلوم مما مضى أنه متى برز النداء من قبله تعالى في ذلك المقام الذي ترى فيه كل أمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive reading describes fear being removed from their hearts; the expression can denote removal, as in clearing an eye of a mote.
rows.anchor: حتى الجماعة بالبناء للمجهول , وأزل هو سبحانه الفزع في قراءة ابن عامر ويعقوب

rows.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read actively that God removes the terror, showing that nothing escapes His command.
rows.anchor: وأزل هو سبحانه الفزع في قراءة ابن عامر ويعقوب , إشارة إلى أنه لا يخرج عن أمره شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the terror subsides, the angels ask one another what their Lord said, recalling His kindness to restore hope and calm their hearts.
rows.anchor: ذاكرين صفة الإحسان ليرجع إليهم رجاؤهم فتسكن لذلك قلوبهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike earthly rulers, God's settled decree cannot be revised or overturned by a powerful courtier; His answer is the unchangeable truth.
rows.anchor: أخبر أن الملك الديان ليس كذلك فقال : { قالوا الحق } أي الثابت الذي لا يمكن أن يبدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the Highest because every rank is below Him, and the Great because none can oppose His judgment; His lack of deficient knowledge means He speaks only truth.
rows.anchor: فلا يقول غير الحق من نقص علم { الكبير } أي الذي لا كبير غيره فيعارضه في شيء من حكم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when God decrees in heaven, angels submit with their wings; after the terror lifts they confirm the true word, which jinn steal and pass down to soothsayers, sometimes before a meteor strikes, mixing it with a hundred lies.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( إذا قضى الله الأمر في السماء ضربت الملائكة بأجنحتها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Masruq reports from Ibn Masud that when God speaks revelation the heavens hear it, then after the sound and fear cease the angels know it is truth and ask what their Lord said.
rows.anchor: وقال مسروق عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما : ( وإذا تكلم الله بالوحي سمع أهل السماوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says each clan of jinn had a station in heaven where they heard revelation, then relayed what they heard to soothsayers, who sometimes found their predictions true.
rows.anchor: وروى لكل قبيل من الجن مقعد من السماء يسمعون فيه الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Prophet was sent, the jinn were driven away; Arabs feared the heavenly residents had perished and sacrificed camels until Thaqif stopped them, while Satan's army traced the event to Mecca by smelling earth.
rows.anchor: فلما بعث الله رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم دحروا , فقالت العرب : هلك من في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question identifies the misguided worshippers as those who worshipped the angels; the cited parallel is Jesus being asked whether he told people to take him and his mother as gods.
rows.anchor: [ المائدة : 116 ] الآيات : { أهؤلاء } أي الضالون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphasis on “you alone” means only exclusive, sincere worship counts, warning Quraysh against treating anything else as valid worship.
rows.anchor: وأشار إلى أنه لا ينفع من العبادة إلا ما كان خالصا فقال : { إياكم } أي خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels begin their disavowal with glorification and humility, fearing God's punishment.
rows.anchor: مفتتحين بالتنزيه تخضعا بين يدي البراءة خوفا من حلول السطوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Glory be to You” declares that no one besides God merits worship.
rows.anchor: ننزهك تنزيها يليق بجلالك عن أن يستحق أحد غيرك أن يعبد .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is the angels' deity and bond; every aspect of guardianship, including knowledge and power, belongs to Him, so the angels cannot turn to distant, powerless worshippers.
rows.anchor: أي معبودنا الذي لا وصلة بيننا وبين أحد إلا بأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels have no guardianship relationship with the worshippers, only enmity; those who draw near to others through disobedience have their hearts hardened and come to hate them.
rows.anchor: ليس بيننا وبينهم من ولاية , بل عداوة , وكذا كل من تقرب إلى شخص بمعصية الله يقسي الله قلبه عليه ويبغضه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People in fact worshipped the jinn, Iblis and his descendants, who dressed up angel worship without the angels' consent; jinn spoke from idols and were sought for refuge in frightening places, like those enslaved to money or fine cloth.
rows.anchor: أي إبليس وذريته الذين زينوا لهم عبادتنا من غير رضانا بذلك , وكانوا يدخلون في أجواف الأصنام ويخاطبونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people firmly believe in the jinn through shirk and intend them in worship; a few accept other beings decorated by jinn, but the true object is still the jinn, whose soothsayer reports they credit despite frequent lies.
rows.anchor: أي راسخون في الإشتراك لا يقصدون بعبادتهم غيرهم , وقليل منهم من يقصد بعبادته بتزيين الجن وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the idolaters' arguments and attachments fail, the Judgment rebuke says no one, whether near or far, can secure benefit or harm for another; benefit is named first because intercession is the context.
rows.anchor: ولما بطلت تمسكاتهم , وتقطعت تعلقاتهم , تسبب عن ذلك تقريعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God removes the worldly ability of creatures to benefit or harm one another, fully displaying His sovereignty alone in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: نسلب الخلائق ما كنا مكناهم منه في الدنيا من التنافع والتضارر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers who put worship in the wrong place, especially those denying resurrection, are told to taste the Fire they habitually denied.
rows.anchor: أي بوضع العبادة في غير موضعها ولا سيما من ضم إلى ذلك إنكار المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Long exposure breeds familiarity, and love of what is familiar kills by making people persist in it, explaining why the decree has settled over most of them.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تطاول الإقامة على شيء موجبا للإلف له , والإلف قتال لما يوجب من الإصرار على المألوف لمحبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The settled decree is punishment earned through persistent heedlessness; most do not believe the warning and instead grow more arrogant and scheming.
rows.anchor: وهو إيجاب العذاب بملازمة الغفلة { على أكثرهم فهم } أي بسبب ذلك { لا يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The neck shackles represent the darkness of misguidance in this life, while in the afterlife the image becomes an actual visible form.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكر هو اليوم معنى ومثال وفي الآخرة ذات ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collar reaches the chin, the point where the jaws meet, so its heaviness prevents the head from bowing; its upward reach is specified because the downward effect would be obvious.
rows.anchor: جمع ذقن وهو مجتمع اللحيين , فهي لذلك مانهة من مطاطأة الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their lifted heads resemble an arrogant posture, but they are compelled to it, making apparent pride inward abasement.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا من رفع الرأس فعل المتكبر , وكان تكبرهم في غير موضعه , بين تعالى أنهم ملجؤون إليه فهو ذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form “muqmaḥūn” means they are made to lift their heads and lower their gaze, like a camel that raises its head and refuses to drink.
rows.anchor: من أقمح الرجل - إذا أقمحه غيره أي جعله قامحا أي رافعا رأسه غاضا بصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bishr ibn Abi Hazim is introduced as the poet of a verse describing a ship, cited from the lexicon compendium as evidence for this posture.
rows.anchor: قال في الجمع بين العباب والمحكم : قال بشر بن أبي حازم يصف سفينة ,

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan cites a verse in which people lower their gaze beside a dead body like thirsty camels that raise their heads, illustrating “al-qimāḥ.”
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : ميتة أحدهم ليدفنها : ونحن على جوانبها قعود نغض الطرف كالإبل القماح

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi defines “al-qamḥ” as the camel posture of striking the head back toward its back.
rows.anchor: وقال الرازي في اللوامع : والقمح : الذي يضرب رأسه إلى ظهره هيئة البعير

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz says “al-muqmaḥ” describes someone staring with raised head.
rows.anchor: وقال القزاز : والمقمح : الشاخص بعيينه الرافع رأسه .

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr says a “qāmiḥ” camel refuses water despite intense thirst and inability to bring itself to drink.
rows.anchor: أبو عمرو : والقامح من الإبل هو الذي لا يشرب وهو عطشان عطشا شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source also records “qamḥ” as a verbal noun and “iqtiḥām” as taking something in the palm and swallowing it, with “qamḥa” like a bite or mouthful.
rows.anchor: والقمح مصدر قمحت الشيء والاقتماح : أخذك الشيء في راحتك ثم تقمحه في فيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that they raise their heads arrogantly to avoid looking toward the caller and would retreat into the sky if they could.
rows.anchor: رفع رؤوسهم عن النظر إلى الداعي تكبرا بحيث لو أمكنهم أن يسكنوا الجو لهم يتأخروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they abandon a great good that deserves their attention despite needing it, like a thirsty camel prevented by an unseen restraint from drinking.
rows.anchor: أو لأنهم يتركون هذا الأمر العظيم الحسن الجدير بأن تقبل عليه ويتروى منه وهم في غاية الحاجة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive participle indicates that they are overpowered and made to miss this great benefit.
rows.anchor: ولذلك بنى الاسم للمفعول إشارة إلى أنهم مقهورون على تفويت حظهم من هذا الأمر الجليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a raised head by itself does not prevent forward vision, God also sets a barrier in front of them.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الرافع رأسه غير ممنوع من النظر أمامه قال : { وجعلنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barrier in front blocks the direction they can know, and the one behind blocks what is hidden from them; the repeated word stresses that both barriers are real and leave no direction to turn toward truth.
rows.anchor: أي فصارت كل جهة يلتفت إليها منسدة , فصاروا لذلك لا يمكنهم النظر إلى الحق ولا الخلوص إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine covering over their eyes prevents them from seeing truth or benefit with either outward sight or inner insight.
rows.anchor: أي جعلنا على أبصارهم بما لنا من العظمة غشاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They do not see” means there can be no renewed perception of truth or what benefits them, externally or inwardly.
rows.anchor: أي لا يتجدد لهم هذا الوصف من إبصار الحق وما ينفعهم ببصر ظاهر وبصيرة باطنة أصلا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After noting the loss of sight, the author turns to hearing; “equal” means absolutely no difference whether the Prophet warns them or not.
rows.anchor: ولما منعوا بذلك حس البصر , أخبر عن حس السمع فقال : { وسواء } أي مستو ومعتدل غاية الاعتدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition of elevation underscores their lack of reason: if they resist even under the highest warning, they resist others more.
rows.anchor: وزاد في الدلالة على عدم عقولهم بالتعبير بأداة الاستعلاء إيذانا بأنهم إذا امتنعوا مع المستعلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure to believe is caused by a like impediment to hearing; the revealer is mighty, so when He acts there is no way around it.
rows.anchor: علم أن السبب المانع من السمع مثله , لأن المخبر عزيز , فهو إذا فعل شيئا كان على وجه لا يمكن فيه حيلة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a warning that the hearer benefits from and that leads to salvation is meant; in effect, only one who believes benefits from the Prophet's warning.
rows.anchor: أي إنذارا ينتفع به المنذر فيتأثر عنه النجاة , فالمعنى : إنما يؤمن بإنذارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the Reminder means striving to follow everything that recalls God, including the Quran and other reminders that ennoble their recipient.
rows.anchor: أي أجهد نفسه في اتباع كل ما يذكر بالله من القرآن وغيره ويذكر به صاحبه ويشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fear the All-Merciful intensely; the shift from the expression of majesty to mercy shows that reminders of God's kindness suffice to teach the fearful.
rows.anchor: ودل لفت الكلام عن مظهر العظمة إلى الوصف بالرحمانية على أن أهل الخشية يكفيهم في الاتعاظ التذكير بالإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing God unseen means believing in unseen powers, especially resurrection, without demanding a sign that removes the veil and turns faith into direct witnessing; fear also includes the possibility of punishment or lost favor.
rows.anchor: أي بسبب ما يخبر به من مقدوراته الغائبة لا سيما البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen fear is also sincere fear when no human observer is present to impress.
rows.anchor: ويخشاه أيضا خشية خالصة في حال غيبته عمن يرائيه من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are the guided God-fearing people; others cannot be set right, so the Prophet should grieve no more than his duty to warn, while God knows who is receptive and who is hardened.
rows.anchor: فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات , فإنه ليس عليك إلا الإنذار , إن الله عليم بما يصنعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “give him good news” follows the singular form “whoever” and signals how few such people are in this comprehensive, heart-like surah.
rows.anchor: فقال مفردا الضمير على النسق الماضي في مراعاة لفظ ( من ) دلالة على قلة هذا الصنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness covers even grave and repeatedly committed sins; repeated return to sin and repentance does not prevent a person from having true fear of God.
rows.anchor: أي لذنوبه وإن عظمت وإن تكررت مواقعته لها وتوبته منها , فإن ذلك لا يمنع الاتصاف بالخشية .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generous reward is an immense, pleasant, continuous abode with no discomfort.
rows.anchor: أي دار عظيم هنيء لذيذ متواصل , لا كدر فيه بوجه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Gardeners have fruit exclusively, and it never runs out or becomes inaccessible to them.
rows.anchor: أي لا تنقطع أبدا , فلا مانع لهم من تناولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever they seek is granted: it may be unspoken wishes arising in the heart, such as foods and drinks, or, if it means God's speech, an expression of special care.
rows.anchor: إما إخراجا لما قد يهجس في النفس من غير عزم عليه إن كان المراد في الجنة من غير كلام الله كالمآكل والمشارب ونحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified wording can encompass answered requests in this life and the next; they had restrained worldly desires, turning toward enduring righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: أعري الكلام من الظرف ليفهم إجابة دعائهم في الدنيا وإنالتهم جميع مرادهم في الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author glosses “they ask for” as seeking something with longing, either continuing the account of their requests or introducing the next statement.
rows.anchor: ثم فسر يدعونه - أي يطلبونه - بغاية الاشتياق إليه أو استأنف الإخبار عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Peace” is an immense, indescribable greeting to the people of Paradise, encompassing every blessing; it may be an existent peace or something spoken.
rows.anchor: أي عظيم جدا لا يكتنه وصفه , عليكم يا أهل الجنة , كائن هو أو مقول هو , والسلام يجمع جميع النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting is speech from the Lord, the ever-beneficent and immensely generous; its delight combines greeting and vision, sustains them through awe, and qualifies them for this honored station despite their limited worthiness.
rows.anchor: في حال السلام وسماع الكلام بلذة الرؤية مع التقوية عن الدهش والصعق لعظيم الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context indicates that God speaks this greeting directly, without an intermediary, emphasized by “saying,” the initial preposition, and the attributes of kindness.
rows.anchor: وقد أوضح هذا السياق أنه من الله تعالى بلا واسطة , فإنه أكده بالقول وحرف الابتداء

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says nothing equals this bliss in joy, comfort, honor, and exalted status, and it is the true purpose of that day's blessings.
rows.anchor: كما قال الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري : ولا ارتياب في أنه لا شيء يعدل هذا في النعيم وقرة العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse is the heart of the day's blessings and, as the heart of the heart-like Quranic surah, the heart of the surah itself.
rows.anchor: فصح أن هذه الآية قلب قلب هذه السورة كما كانت هذه السورة قلب القرآن

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: A report attributed through Jabir is cited to support the claim that the greeting comes directly from God, without an intermediary.
rows.anchor: أنه من الله تعالى بلا واسطة عن جابر رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jabir reports that while the people of Paradise enjoy their bliss a light shines and the Lord appears, greets them with peace, and looks at them as they look at Him; they ignore every other blessing while seeing Him, and His light and blessing remain in their homes after He is veiled.
rows.anchor: قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( بينا أهل الجنة في نعيمهم إذ سطع لهم نور

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان الصابوني
rows.claim: Abu Uthman al-Sabuni grades the report as unusual in both chain and text and says he knows it only from this route.
rows.anchor: قال الاستاذ أبو عثمان : هذا حديث غريب الإسناد والمتن لا أعلم إني كتبته إلا من هذا الوجه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Separate” commands a deliberate, complete separation, and “today” heightens the terror of the scene.
rows.anchor: أي انفردوا انفرادا هو بغاية القصد , وجرى على النمط الماضي من زيادة التهويل لذلك الموقف بإعادة قوله : { اليوم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are separated either from God's righteous servants or from those still in the assembly, so the righteous can be rid of their filth and harm; freedom from an observer and from an enemy completes joy.
rows.anchor: لأن غيبة الرقيب أتم النعيم , وإبعاد العدو أعلى السرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted vocative particle does not suggest intimacy; it shows that the criminals are wholly within God's grasp with no barrier to His disposal of them.
rows.anchor: وحذف أداة النداء لا لقرب الكرامة بل للدلالة على أنهم في القبضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are deeply rooted in crime and must not imagine they will mix with believers; their worldly prideful separation from believers is now reversed.
rows.anchor: أي العريقون في الإجرام , فلا يقع في أوهامكم أنكم تخالطونهم اليوم أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between what is said to criminals and believers benefits one group and harms the other, completing the righteous' welfare.
rows.anchor: فهذا قوله للمجرمين وذلك قوله للمؤمنين , فصح أنه قلب لأنه به صلاح بعض المكلفين وفساد الآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author points readers to a dream mentioned near the beginning of Surat al-Rum as relevant to this scene.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في أوائل سورة الروم منام ينفع استحضاره هنا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals separate at once, concealing their regret while showing it through biting fingers, grinding teeth, staring eyes, grimaces, lowered heads, pale faces, and being dragged on their faces.
rows.anchor: وأسروا الندامة وسقط في أيديهم فعضوا الأنامل , وصروا بالأسنان , وشخصت منهم الأبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rebukes them because He did not leave them neglected: He gave them intellect and sufficient proofs, sent messengers, and revealed scriptures to show the path to salvation.
rows.anchor: بما نصبت من الأدلة , ومنحت من العقول , وبعثت من الرسل , وأنزلت من الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression “Did I not charge you?” means a solemn, emphatic admonition through the evidence, intellect, messengers, and scriptures that explain the road to salvation.
rows.anchor: أي أوصيكم إيصاء عظيما بما نصبت من الأدلة , ومنحت من العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker shifts from the aspect of benevolence to first-person singular speech to avoid ambiguity, then points to God's loftiness, majesty, and perfection.
rows.anchor: لافِتا القول عن مظهر الإحسان إلى ما هو أولى به من مظهر التكلم بالوحدة دفعا للبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans receive the address because this surah is the heart, the heart is the noblest organ, and humans are the noblest creatures; addressing them also addresses the jinn.
rows.anchor: وكان الإنسان أشرف الموجودات , خصه بالخطاب لأنه خطابه خطاب للجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording further emphasizes the human addressee's lofty rank and immense station through the sign of distance.
rows.anchor: فقال مؤكدا ما أفهمه حرف الغاية من علو رتبته , وعظيم منزلته بما أشارت إليه أداة البعد :
